newsitem.title: UK: BRADY BONDS FIRM BUT TRADE LIMITED AHEAD OF DATA.
newsitem.headline: BRADY BONDS FIRM BUT TRADE LIMITED AHEAD OF DATA.

text.p: Dollar-denominated emerging market debt was firm on Thursday, gaining with U.S. Treasuries, but dealers said business was held in check by caution ahead of key U.S. data.
"Prices have been marked up with (U.S.) bonds but there is no real trading. Russia is better bid on the back on good local demand for Min Fins," said one.
After well-received U.S. July retail sales on Wednesday, all eyes are now focused on July's Consumer Price Index at 1230 GMT.
"If we get more benign figures today we should see further gains in longer duration Latins," said one debt analyst.
Brazil's top-trading "C" bond gained 1/8 to 83-1/4 bid. Mexico's UMS 2026 added to New York gains to stand 1/8 higher at 120-3/4.
Russian debt pushed to new highs, after retreating slightly on Wednesday, as good local demand continued to drive the market higher on optimism about the country's London Club debt restructuring.
Venshekonombank loans put on 3/8 to 102-1/4 while PRINs gained 1/8 to 74-1/8, IANs added 3/8 to 81-18 and the Min Fin series was bid between 1/8 and 1/4 higher.
Elsewhere in Eastern Europe, Polish Pars were a full point firmer at 58-7/8.

"The Brady market was stable in the face of the big sell-off in Treasuries and now the slide has stopped on Treasuries that seems to be an endorsement of their performance," said an economist at a U.S. investment bank.
